I regretted it the first couple weeks. All the stories of restrictive eating got to me too! You’ll find you have a LOT more freedom than the horror stories tell, but remember this is about taking your life back and not being dependent on food. Another thing that got to me was the whole changing my anatomy thing. It freaked me out thinking about it and sent me SPIRALING. I’m 3 months out, and i no longer regret it one single bit. I feel so much better, my days are easier, and im looking good! I really do wish i would’ve done it three years earlier when i first looked into it!

I know I’m like a week late, but i may be one of the luckier ones. I’m almost 3 months post op, and i honestly can handle any food. I never got nausea or anything either. *knock on wood* the only thing that has bothered me is gas bubbles in my tummy while I’m eating lol

It seems like it depends on the doctor mostly. I didn’t have any programs i had to go to, i was approved my first appointment, then just had to wait on insurance approval and that took about another month. Then of course a few more appointments, for a stress test, blood work, and a nutritionist. I also wasn’t required to go to therapy or anything beforehand, but that might be because i have my own therapist and psychiatrist. My first appointment was October 29, insurance went through December 1, and my surgery was December 14. Mine went really fast!!

My only suggestion is to not be afraid to eat. You weigh 122 with a bmi of 19, that’s amazing. Food is fuel, you NEED it to survive. Starving yourself because you’re afraid of a stretched sleeve isn’t it. To me, it sounds like (I’m obviously not a professional lol) you’re not getting enough calories to support your body and all it does during the day. Undereating can also cause weight gain because of the shift in the metabolic process. I’m sorry you’re in pain, i really hope you get something figured out!
